chapters.exactFinalPrompt:
Create one independent full-resolution landscape illustration for Pliny the Elder, Naturalis Historia, Book XXI, Chapter 8, “FABRICS WHICH RIVAL THE COLOURS OF FLOWERS.” Historical-scene mode, grounded in Pliny’s comparison of luxurious Roman-dyed fabrics with the scarlet, amethystine, violet, mallow-purple, and yellow colours found in flowers.

COMPOSITION: one continuous sunlit Roman dyer’s courtyard seen from a high three-quarter viewpoint, with textile action dominating the scene and no garden-page repetition. Place exactly two complete ancient Roman textile workers. Near centre-left, one fully visible standing dyer lifts and turns a single long, complete amethyst-violet cloth so its natural S-shaped folds catch the light beside exactly one compact, island-like, fully visible rooted clump of purple mallow; a complete ring of bare paving must surround that flower clump. At lower-right middle ground, a second fully visible kneeling dyer gathers one complete rich scarlet cloth from a shallow, fully visible round dye basin; show the whole cloth from basin to both finished hems, never disappearing beyond the frame. Behind them, one short freestanding drying rail—both posts, feet, crossbar, and rope entirely inside the image—holds exactly two additional complete fabrics separated by open air: one restrained deep Tyrian crimson-purple length and one small warm yellow bridal veil. Arrange the four fabrics as moving, folded, irregular physical textiles in one shared courtyard, not as equal rectangles, samples, panels, flags, or a colour chart. Add exactly one second compact, island-like, fully visible rooted flower clump containing a few scarlet anemones and pale saffron crocuses, entirely surrounded by bare paving and well away from every edge, plus only two complete plain ceramic dye jars. Leave a broad wedge of quiet sunlit paving as intentional negative space. Every person, hand, foot, cloth hem, rail foot, basin rim, jar, flower clump, and cast shadow must be wholly visible with generous breathing room at every edge. Keep every corner and the entire bottom strip as uninterrupted clean paving, free of objects, plants, brush-like marks, or stray forms.

SHARED PLINIAN FOLIO GRAMMAR: an original deluxe Roman natural-history folio illustration rendered directly across warm full-bleed aged vellum; iron-gall linework; fine cross-hatching, stipple, and dry-brush texture; restrained mineral pigments only—umber, lampblack, muted verdigris, faded lapis, madder, and ochre. Ancient, timeless, beautiful, tactile, rough and polished at once. Landscape 3:2, native 1536x1024. Let the textile folds carry restrained madder, faded lapis-violet, ochre-yellow, and crimson-purple accents against a quieter umber courtyard. Matte physical-media appearance, never photographic or glossy digital.

ABSOLUTE EXCLUSIONS: no text, letters, captions, labels, numerals, pseudo-writing, calligraphy, inscriptions, scrolls, open books, signatures, signature-like squiggles, logos, watermarks, stray corner marks, modern objects, modern clothing, sewing machines, photography, glossy digital rendering, decorative page border, visible sheet edge, torn parchment, blank paper held by a figure, split panels, diptychs, triptychs, collages, swatch charts, repeated crops, repeated identical frames, duplicated figures, floating cloth, cropped or clipped primary subjects. No ceremonial bride, no medicinal treatment, no ingestion, no violence.
chapters.visualQaNotes: Inspected at original 1536x1024 resolution. Exactly two complete textile workers handle one complete amethyst cloth and one complete scarlet cloth; the fully contained freestanding rail carries the complete Tyrian crimson-purple fabric and yellow veil. Both compact flower clumps, both jars, the dye basin, every cloth hem, rail foot and shadow are inside the frame. The courtyard reads as one physical scene rather than swatches or panels. No text, pseudo-writing, repeated frame, modern object, floating textile or clipped primary subject was found.
